tools_used: CourtListener MCP read_document (Kentucky Supreme Court opinion below)
helpful: The provisioned petition, brief in opposition, and QP text were the decisive inputs: the BIO's vehicle arguments (invited error, adequate-and-independent state ground, record failure) are the whole affirmance/DIG tail, and they were readable without retrieval.

Reading the opinion below through the MCP server sharpened the reversed-versus-vacated call: the Kentucky court decided the threshold on exactly two factors and never reached strict scrutiny, which is the shape the Court usually reverses rather than vacates.
The statpack merits table with its excluded-count guard made the baseline pooling mechanical.
gaps: fedcourts query has no subject or keyword filter on SCOTUS rows, so it cannot surface doctrinal neighbors (the Court's prior RLUIPA and RFRA merits cases); the ranked result for a granted/2020s query was dominated by shadow-docket applications rather than argued cases.

The merits statpack section carries no cut by lower-court type (state high court vs. federal circuit) or by subject area, so the adjustment from the pooled rate to a religious-liberty petitioner's rate is unquantified judgment.
CourtListener held no text for the Third Circuit's Anash v. Borough of Kingston opinion the BIO flagged as a post-petition split development, so its characterization rests on the BIO alone.
notes: Merits grant-moment cell, forward mode. No merits briefs on disk, as the moment requires. Retrieval used about seven calls, well under the advisory budget.
